title: Analog In, Out Serial
description: A knob controls how bright an LED is — and the numbers show on the Serial Monitor.

source.title: Arduino docs: Analog In Out Serial

steps.clip: Grab an Arduino Uno and its USB cable, a breadboard, 10 kΩ potentiometer (knob), 220 Ω resistor, LED and a few jumper wires.
Push the knob into the breadboard so each of its three legs is in a different numbered column.
hints: The two outer legs are for power; the middle leg gives the reading.
Two legs in the same column would be joined, so use three different columns.
steps.goal: Put the knob on the breadboard.

steps.clip: A jumper wire from one outer leg's column to the − (blue) row along the bottom edge — and, since this is the first thing using it, one more wire from that − row to a GND pin on the Arduino (now the whole row is GND).
hints: Either outer leg works — swapping them only reverses which way is 'more'.
steps.goal: Connect one outer leg to GND.

steps.clip: A jumper wire from the other outer leg's column to the + (red) row along the bottom edge — and, since this is the first thing using it, one more wire from that + row to the 5V pin on the Arduino (now the whole row is 5V).
hints: Now the knob has 0 V at one end and 5 V at the other.
steps.goal: Connect the other outer leg to 5V.

steps.clip: A jumper wire from the middle leg's column to pin A0 on the Arduino.
hints: A0 is on the Arduino's ANALOG IN header.
The middle leg's voltage follows the knob: 0 V to 5 V.
steps.goal: Connect the knob's middle leg to A0.

steps.clip: Push a 220 Ω resistor into the breadboard, its two legs in two different numbered columns (leave some space from the last part).
hints: A resistor works either way round.
It protects the LED: without it too much current flows and the LED burns out.
steps.goal: Put the resistor for the LED on the breadboard.

steps.clip: A jumper wire from one of the resistor's columns to pin 9 on the Arduino.
hints: Pin 9 is on the Arduino's row of numbered sockets.
Any free hole in that column works.

steps.clip: Now the LED: its long leg in the same column as the resistor's other leg, its short leg in an empty column right next to it.
hints: The long leg is + (the anode) — it must face the resistor or the LED stays dark.
Legs in the same column are already connected.
steps.goal: Connect the LED's long leg (+) to the resistor.

steps.clip: A jumper wire from the short leg's column to the − (blue) row.
hints: The − row is already joined to GND.
steps.goal: Connect the LED's short leg (−) to GND.

steps.clip: Copy the code into the Arduino IDE and click Upload. Turn the knob: the LED gets brighter and dimmer, and the Serial Monitor shows both numbers.
